active_work_package.title: Platform repository skeleton from the P0.2 design
active_work_package.objective: Create the place every later package lands, shaped so the modular monolith boundaries are tested rather than intended: the workspace and layout, the module registry, the seven dependency rules generated from it, the migration lint, the boundary test suite that proves both fire, the charter, these records and their schemas, and the CI skeleton. It implements no epic and creates no domain table.

stop_reason: Independent peer review has now returned REVISION_REQUIRED three times, and the third round is closed here. Two of its findings were total fail-open holes. In the migration lint, one apostrophe inside a double-quoted identifier made scrub() blank everything up to the next apostrophe in the file, so a migration hid a cross-schema table, DROP SCHEMA audit CASCADE, a P0 domain table and a table with no tenant_id between two such names and the lint reported PASS: four protections failing open at once, on legal SQL. In the record validator, the authority registry could be forged five different ways, each of them legal YAML - a flow-style mapping, a section named in capitals, tab or three-space indentation, and an entry with no status line - and each forged p0_implementation, the grant this repository exists to withhold, with exit 0. The lint is now a single-pass scanner that refuses what it cannot represent; the authority reader's default is an error rather than a skip. Beyond those: a migration file the lint never opened is refused rather than skipped, badf/gates.yaml and two statements of badf/lifecycle.yaml are validated, a Work Package can no longer enter ACCEPTED ahead of its acceptance grant, and scripts/coverage-gate.mjs now fails the build when a protection this repository names is witnessed by no fixture - which is the defect all three rounds actually found, in three different instruments. WP-001 stays at ENGINEERING_READY. Two agent reviewers returned these findings; neither is the independent human verifier the P0.2 design names, and no re-review of this head has happened. NS-001 is now half done and stays primary: branch protection is applied and negative control 6 is observed for the first time, recorded in evidence/security-proof/negative-control-6.md, but its other half - a named human holding the repository-administrator seat - is not, and badf/agents.yaml has no field capable of holding one.
known_divergence: The boundary rules here are the PROPOSAL of a design at IN_REVIEW that depends on five ADRs, all DRAFT_REQUIRED; if ADR-001 narrows or widens the seven rules, the registry and the generator change with it and the suite is re-run. A CLAIM THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY MADE IS WITHDRAWN AS FALSE, not softened. It said the round-two response was to invert the default rather than extend the list, and gave the authority parser as an instance. The authority parser was an allow-list of five section names sitting on a reader whose default was to skip the line, which is the extend-the-list pattern the same sentence claimed had been rejected. The lesson was stated correctly and not applied to the fix that shipped alongside it, and round three walked through the gap five ways. Two smaller claims are withdrawn with it: the checkpoint said 110 tracked files where the commit held 132, and completed_scope claimed one violation shape per fixture while one fixture carried ten. What the three rounds have in common is not a weak rule. It is that THE INSTRUMENT WAS CONSISTENTLY STRONGER THAN ITS EVIDENCE: four dependency rules loosenable with no fixture going red, two controls surviving their own rule being disabled, then three of four audit verbs and two of four domain words named in AGENTS.md section 5 and witnessed by nothing at all. scripts/coverage-gate.mjs attacks that class rather than its instances, and derives what must be witnessed from the code so the list cannot drift from the rules. One gap is NOT closed and is the most important line here: a forgery that edits badf/authority.yaml, badf/current-state.json and the checkpoint CONSISTENTLY still passes every check in this repository, because nothing here binds a record to a human identity. No validator can close that. The mechanism that addresses it is the branch protection applied under NS-001, where a second person must approve the change, and that is now real rather than conventional for the first time.
